name: manual_4e38d1
claim: Even with file-disjoint parallel agent dispatch (each job assigned a distinct set of files), a follow-up direct edit to a file that job is still actively refining can race: reading the file's tail output once and then Edit-ing it later based on that stale read can silently merge on top of content the dispatched job wrote AFTER your read, producing a coherent-looking but unverified final state. The Edit tool's own warning (file changed on disk since last read) is the signal to stop and re-Read fresh before trusting the diff, not just proceed because the edit applied without a hard conflict.

decisions.notes: Hit during PR #280 round 2: after reading a dispatched cursor-agent job's tail output showing a find-based grep fix, I Edit-ed the file to add vendor-dir exclusions -- the tool warned the file had other changes not in my context. The job had self-corrected to a superior git-ls-files-based approach in the meantime. Caught only because I re-ran the actual acceptance-check commands myself afterward rather than trusting either my edit or the job's self-report.
